title: GDPR data retention: anonymize old confirmed bookings, delete old pending/cancelled bookings
tech: Node/TypeScript backend only -- no new dependency, no frontend change needed (see below for why)
keyConstraints: Two independent, time-based retention rules, both anchored on booking.start_at (the appointment date/time), decided with Ville: (1) ANONYMIZE: bookings with status = 'confirmed' and start_at older than 3 months -- replace the associated customers row's name, email, AND phone (Ville confirmed email should be included, not just name+phone as originally stated) with the fixed placeholder 'Poistettu GDPR-syistä'. The booking row itself, and all its non-personal fields (service_id, start_at, end_at, status, created_at, confirmed_at), are KEPT untouched -- only the customer's identity is scrubbed. (2) DELETE: bookings with status IN ('pending', 'cancelled') and start_at older than 1 month -- Ville's reasoning: these never resulted in a real appointment, so the data has no ongoing value and should be purged outright rather than anonymized in place. Confirmed by reading the schema (backend/src/db/migrations/) that customers rows are NEVER shared/deduplicated across bookings -- insertCustomer in bookingService.ts always does a plain INSERT with no ON CONFLICT/dedup lookup, so every booking has its own dedicated customers row -- meaning both rules above can safely act on a single booking's data without any risk of affecting a different booking belonging to the same real-world person. IMPORTANT SCHEMA DEPENDENCY for the DELETE rule, confirmed by reading every migration file: customer_booking_tokens.booking_id REFERENCES bookings(id) with NO ON DELETE CASCADE (default RESTRICT), and bookings.customer_id REFERENCES customers(id) similarly RESTRICT -- so deleting a booking requires deleting in dependency order within one transaction: (a) customer_booking_tokens rows for that booking, (b) email_jobs rows for that booking (see below -- not a real FK, matched via JSONB), (c) the bookings row itself, (d) the now-unreferenced customers row. Getting this order wrong will throw a foreign-key violation, not silently corrupt data, but should still be gotten right the first time. EMAIL_JOBS -- confirmed with Ville this is in scope: backend/src/db/types.ts's BookingEmailPayload (used by every customer-facing email job type) stores customerName and customerEmail in plain text in email_jobs.payload (JSONB), and this is NEVER cleaned up today -- emailWorker.ts's redactSensitiveField only strips the one-time manageUrl/loginUrl token after send, not the name/email. BookingEmailPayload also carries bookingId, so matching rows can be found via payload->>'bookingId'. For the ANONYMIZE rule: scrub customerName/customerEmail within matching email_jobs.payload to the same placeholder (a JSONB update, e.g. via jsonb_set, not a full row delete -- the job's own audit fields like status/sent_at/type should stay). For the DELETE rule: delete the matching email_jobs rows entirely, as part of the same per-booking transaction as the schema-dependency chain above. MasseurLoginLinkEmailPayload and MasseurBookingChangeEmailPayload payload shapes do not contain customer PII and are out of scope. MECHANISM: mirror this codebase's existing background-worker pattern exactly -- see backend/src/services/emailWorker.ts's startEmailWorker (setInterval-based, returns a { stop() } handle) and its one-line wiring in backend/src/server.ts. A new retention worker should follow the same shape: a pure, testable 'process once' function (taking an injectable reference time, defaulting to new Date(), so tests don't depend on wall-clock time or need to fake global timers -- follow whatever pattern this codebase already uses for testing time-based logic, e.g. as established in task 024's past-slot-exclusion work) plus a thin startXWorker(intervalMs) wrapper wired into server.ts the same way. Unlike the 5-second email-send interval, this doesn't need near-real-time responsiveness -- a long interval (e.g. once every 24h) is appropriate; Architect should decide whether to also run an immediate first pass at startup (the email worker doesn't, but its consequence of a missed poll is a delayed email, not a missed compliance sweep -- worth weighing given this worker's interval is far longer and Railway deploys may restart the process before a full 24h interval ever elapses). SAFETY, given this is the first task in this codebase that performs irreversible data deletion: the process-once function should log a clear summary every run (count anonymized, count deleted, and which booking ids) even though no new DB column tracks this -- so there's a visible audit trail in server logs without adding schema complexity for a low-volume solo-provider app. Architect should also consider whether the function should support being invoked in a dry-run/report-only mode (log what it would do, mutate nothing) so Ville can validate the query logic against real production data once before fully trusting the scheduled version -- given the DELETE path is irreversible, this is a meaningful extra safety margin worth the small amount of extra code, not scope creep. Use Postgres's own INTERVAL arithmetic in the WHERE clauses (start_at < now() - INTERVAL '3 months' / '1 month') rather than a manual day-count approximation, for correct calendar-month handling. No frontend changes are needed or expected -- confirmed by reading AdminDashboard.tsx: customer_name/customer_email/customer_phone are already just JOINed live from the customers table and rendered as plain text, so once a customers row is anonymized the admin UI shows the placeholder automatically with zero frontend code changes, and a deleted booking simply stops appearing in list results.
description: Add a scheduled backend worker that enforces a GDPR-driven data retention policy on old bookings: (1) for confirmed bookings whose appointment date is more than 3 months in the past, anonymize the customer's name, email, and phone number to a fixed placeholder while keeping the booking record itself (service, time, status) for business records; (2) for pending or cancelled bookings whose appointment date is more than 1 month in the past, delete the booking and all associated personal data entirely, since it never resulted in a real appointment. Also close the gap where customer name/email persist indefinitely in the sent-email log (email_jobs), which would otherwise silently defeat the anonymization.
acceptanceCriteria: A confirmed booking with start_at more than 3 months in the past has its customers row's name, email, and phone all replaced with 'Poistettu GDPR-syistä'; the booking row itself (service_id, start_at, end_at, status, timestamps) is unchanged and still present
A confirmed booking with start_at less than 3 months in the past is never touched

A pending or cancelled booking with start_at more than 1 month in the past is deleted entirely, along with its customer_booking_tokens rows and its customers row, in the correct dependency order (no foreign-key violations)
A pending or cancelled booking with start_at less than 1 month in the past is never touched

email_jobs rows matching an anonymized booking (via payload->>'bookingId') have customerName/customerEmail scrubbed to the placeholder within their JSONB payload, with the rest of the payload and the job's own status/timestamps untouched
email_jobs rows matching a deleted booking are deleted entirely, in the same transaction as the rest of that booking's deletion
email_jobs rows for MasseurLoginLinkEmailPayload/MasseurBookingChangeEmailPayload job types (no customer PII) are never touched by either rule

The retention sweep is implemented as a testable 'process once' function with an injectable reference time (not dependent on real wall-clock time in tests), plus a setInterval-based worker wired into server.ts, mirroring emailWorker.ts's existing pattern
Each run logs a clear summary (counts + affected booking ids) for both the anonymize and delete paths
Running the process twice in a row (idempotency check) produces no errors and no further changes the second time

New unit/integration tests covering: a confirmed booking just past the 3-month threshold gets anonymized; one just under the threshold does not; a pending/cancelled booking just past the 1-month threshold gets fully deleted (booking + tokens + customer + matching email_jobs); one just under does not; matching email_jobs payloads are correctly scrubbed vs. deleted per the two rules; non-customer-PII job types are never touched
No regression to any existing backend test -- run the full existing suite, not just an assumed-safe subset
npm test, npm run build, npm run lint, and npx tsc --noEmit all pass in backend/ (frontend unaffected, no frontend files change)
relevantFilePaths: backend/src/services/emailWorker.ts (the existing background-worker pattern to mirror)
backend/src/services/bookingService.ts (insertCustomer -- confirms no customer dedup; read-only reference)

backend/src/db/migrations/ (001_init_core_tables.sql, 002_bookings_and_exclusion_constraint.sql, 007_customer_booking_tokens.sql -- read-only reference for the FK dependency chain; a new migration file may be needed only if the Architect decides new indexes are needed for the retention queries' WHERE clauses, e.g. on bookings.start_at + status, though bookings_provider_start_at_idx already exists)
backend/src/pages equivalent -- N/A, no frontend files expected to change
backend/test/ (new test file for the retention worker, following this codebase's existing test structure/fixtures)
securityConsiderations: This is the first task in this codebase performing irreversible data deletion -- the SECURITY stage should scrutinize the WHERE-clause date arithmetic and the deletion dependency order with extra care, since a logic error here could delete or anonymize the wrong set of bookings with no undo. No new external input or API endpoint is introduced (this is an internal scheduled process, not a new route), so no new AuthN/AuthZ surface. The anonymization/deletion must only ever run against the application's own database via the existing pool -- confirm no new externally-reachable trigger (e.g. an admin-facing button or API route) is introduced unless explicitly decided otherwise; this task is scoped to the automatic background sweep only.
